title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD & Roadmap Q1–Q3 2027
author: Asha Patel
summary: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap themes for Q1–Q3 2027, pricing and packaging proposals, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and GTM planning and will be used as the canonical source for upcoming releases and customer-facing messaging.
overview: Background: Unified Inference is Redwood Inference's cross-environment product that provides a single API and operational model for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Objective: provide a clear set of prioritized capabilities and milestones for Q1–Q3 2027 to drive revenue growth via Dedicated contracts, increase self-serve adoption for Hosted API, and expand Private deployments for regulated customers. Scope: model routing, cost/performance controls, rollout primitives, observability improvements, packaging/pricing updates, and the v2 release of Redwood Optimize.
product_goals:
1) Improve unit economics for high-throughput customers by 20% through batching, caching, and quantization recommendations.
2) Deliver an enterprise-grade private deployment path with automated lifecycle management and KMS/HSM integration.
3) Increase self-serve conversion by streamlining onboarding and adding pricing clarity for mixed-mode usage.
4) Make rollouts robust: canary/A-B + automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants under load.
prd_requirements:
Core functional requirements (priority order):
1. Unified API parity: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, and function/tool calling must behave identically across hosted, dedicated, and private modes (API contract v2).
2. Model routing and fallback: policy engine to route requests by latency, cost, and region with automated fallback to compatible quantized variants.
3. Cost/perf control panel: per-route batching/caching/quantization suggestions and one-click apply.
4. Private deployment lifecycle: installer + upgrade/rollback automation + audit-log export to customer SIEM.
5. Observability: per-model SLOs, token-level cost breakdown, latency histograms with p50/p95/p99.
6. Rollout primitives: canary, gradual traffic shift, automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions.
Non-functional requirements:
- Availability: 99.95% SLA for Dedicated customers.
- Latency: median generation latency <= configured per-tier target (see SLA table).
- Security: KMS integration for Private, TLS everywhere, RBAC for console.
- Scalability: support up to 10k rps for Dedicated pools with autoscaling policies.
Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests across hosted/dedicated/private demonstrate API parity for a representative prompt set.
- Cost recommendations validated on 3 customer workloads with >=10% measured savings.
- Private installer completes automated upgrade with zero-downtime in 90% of test runs.

design_specs:
High-level design notes: 
- Runtime: extend serving runtime to expose model variant metadata (quantization, kernel selection) and per-request routing hints.
- Policy engine: declarative policy format (YAML) with rules evaluated in order: region -> latency target -> cost tier -> customer override.
- Config schema (example):
  apiVersion: v1
  route: /v1/generate
  policy:
    - match: {region: eu-west-1} 
      target: low-latency
    - match: {cost_tier: low} 
      target: low-cost
- Observability: Trace ID must propagate from API gateway through runtime to model container; include token-level timing spans.
- Security: Private installer authenticates against customer KMS, stores keys in HSM-backed keystore, and rotates keys per customer policy.
A set of diagrams (to be attached in page attachments): solution-context, runtime-dataflow, policy-evaluation-flow.
roadmap_and_themes:
Roadmap themes Q1–Q3 2027:
- Q1: Stabilize API parity + basic model routing; release Redwood Optimize v2 alpha for Dedicated customers.
- Q2: Shipping cost/performance control panel, observability enhancements, and first private deployments with KMS integration.
- Q3: Feature complete private lifecycle automation, canary rollouts, pricing packaging updates and GA for Redwood Optimize v2.
Milestones (timeline):
| Quarter | Milestone | Success metric |
| Q1 2027 | API parity beta + routing v1 | 3 pilot customers onboarded |
| Q2 2027 | Optimize v2 beta + cost panel | 20% reduction in average token cost for pilots |
| Q3 2027 | Private lifecycle GA + rollouts | 5 enterprise customers migrated; <1% rollback rate |
pricing_and_packaging:
Proposed packaging (summary):
- Hosted (self-serve): pay-as-you-go per-token with discounted committed tiers; add-on: extended observability retention.
- Dedicated (reserved): monthly commit for GPU pools + overage pricing; SLA tiers (Standard: 99.9%, Premium: 99.95%).
- Private: license + support fee + optional installation service; pricing tier based on node count and retention requirements.
Pricing table (example):
| Plan | Billing model | SLO | Typical customer |
| Hosted | per-token | best-effort | startups, dev/test |
| Dedicated Standard | monthly commit + overage | 99.9% | mid-market apps |
| Dedicated Premium | monthly commit + overage | 99.95% | revenue-critical apps |
| Private | license + support | customer-defined | regulated/enterprise |
Notes on packaging: bundle Redwood Optimize recommendations as a paid add-on for Dedicated and Private customers; include a self-serve Optimize trial for Hosted customers (30 days).
release_notes:
Release: Unified Inference v2027.1 (candidate)
Highlights:
- API: v2 contract published; improved parity across deployment modes.
- Runtime: model routing v1 with fallback to quantized variants under capacity pressure.
- Console: initial cost/performance recommendations and per-route dashboards.
- Private: beta installer with KMS integration (limited customer pilot).
Known issues:
- Edge-case: some long-sequence prompts see increased p99 when fallback is triggered; mitigation: per-route max-seq override.
- UX: pricing calculator in console currently supports only hosted and dedicated; private pricing builder is in progress.
Changelog (technical):
- runtime: add policy-eval endpoint and variant metadata tags.
- api: add model_variant and cost_hint fields.
- console: token-level timing spans and cost breakdown charts.
rollout_and_migration:
Rollout plan (high level):
1) Internal dogfooding (2 weeks): feature flag across staging; run standard eval set and load tests.
2) Pilot customers (4–8 weeks): onboard 3–5 pilot customers across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; collect cost/latency/quality metrics.
3) Gradual ramp (4 weeks): open to early adopter program; monitor SLOs and automatic rollback triggers.
4) GA: wider availability after metric gates met.
Migration guidance for customers: map existing routes -> new API v2 routes, test in canary for 48h, then full migration.
Rollback criteria: sustained SLO breach (p95 latency > target for 15m) OR quality regression (automated eval score drop > configured threshold).
sla_and_metrics:
SLOs and dashboards to monitor: 
- Dedicated Premium: availability 99.95% monthly, p99 generator latency <= 750ms for short-sequence templates.
- Dedicated Standard: availability 99.9% monthly.
- Error budget policy: incidents consuming >25% of monthly error budget require escalation to SRE + customer success.
Key metrics: token cost per 1M tokens, request p50/p95/p99, model cache hit rate, autoscaler thrash rate, rollback frequency.
risks_and_mitigations:
Top risks:
- Risk: Model parity regressions during rollout. Mitigation: expanded integration test matrix + automated quality gates + staged canary.
- Risk: Private installer edge cases across customer environments. Mitigation: partner with field-engineering for 3 initial installs and capture environment matrices.
- Risk: Pricing confusion across mixed-mode customers. Mitigation: build pricing calculator and clear doc examples; include account-level billing samples in Console.
- Risk: Overfitting of cost recommendations causing quality drops. Mitigation: require simulated A/B on production-like workloads before auto-apply and expose rollback.
